title: Simultaneous recording of behavioral and neural responses of free-moving nematodes C. elegans
protocol: Wash nematodes from one 6 cm plate into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube using 1 mL of M9 buffer.
Remove the supernatant and wash again with 1 mL of M9 buffer.
Transfer the nematodes to an NGM condition plate (0, 50, or 100 mM NaCl) with a lawn of E. coli.
Incubate at 20°C overnight for conditioning.
Wash a glass plate, a perforated glass plate, and a PDMS microfluidic chip with 100% ethanol.
Air-dry the washed plates and chip.
Sandwich the PDMS chip between two glass plates.
Align the holes in the perforated glass plate with the holes for inserting the polyethylene tube (φ 0.58 mm) in the PDMS chip.
Insert stainless steel tubes into the four holes of the PDMS chip.
Fix the glass plates together using binder clips.
Vacuum pump for 15 minutes to evaporate.
Mix 0 mM NaCl solution and 100 mM NaCl solution to make 50 mL of 50 mM NaCl solution.
Mix the remaining portion of 0 mM NaCl solution with 100 mM NaCl solution to prepare 25 mM NaCl solution.
Add 0.5 μL of 0.5 μM fluorescein solution to the 25 mM NaCl solution (final concentration: 1 nM).
Put 40 mL each of 50 mM NaCl buffer and 25 mM NaCl buffer into respective 50 mL Terumo syringes.
Set the syringes on the feed pump.
Connect polyethylene tubes to the syringes.
Put 10 mL of 50 mM NaCl buffer into a 10 mL syringe.
Connect the tube to the nematode introduction syringe.
Open and close the flow path using a three-way stopcock.
Attach a syringe with the NaCl solution to one side of the flow path.
Connect a polyethylene tube to the other side for later connection to PDMS.
Attach another syringe to the third flow path to remove air from the tube.
Connect the polyethylene tubes from each syringe and pump to the steel tubes of the PDMS microfluidic device.
Turn on all pumps and open all tubes to allow the solution to flow.
Close all tubes when the chamber is filled with NaCl solution.
Set the flow rate of each pump to 100 μL/min.
Ensure that the solution has completely filled the microfluidic chamber.
Remove any air bubbles present in the chamber if necessary.
Put 1 mL of 50 mM NaCl solution into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Place 10–20 nematodes from the conditioning plate into the NaCl solution using a P1000 micropipette.
Transfer the nematode-containing solution to a nematode-introduction syringe (10 mL Terumo syringe).
Open the tube attached to the nematode-introduction syringe.
Turn on the peristaltic pump for waste fluid.
Introduce nematodes into the microfluidic chamber.
Close the tube from the nematode-introduction syringe after the nematode enters the chamber.
Turn off the waste pump.
Turn on the peristaltic pump for waste and open the tube of 50 mM NaCl solution.
Launch the tracking stage, nematode tracking software, and fluorescence imaging software (MetaMorph).
Select the head of the nematode and start tracking.
Start capturing brightfield and fluorescence images.
Close the tube of 50 mM NaCl solution and simultaneously open the tube of 25 mM NaCl solution 25 seconds after the start of imaging.
Close the tube of 25 mM NaCl solution and open the tube of 50 mM NaCl solution 75 seconds after the start of imaging.
Close the tube of 50 mM NaCl solution again and open the tube of 25 mM NaCl solution at 125 seconds after the start of shooting.
End the measurement, close the tube of 25 mM NaCl solution and open the tube of 50 mM NaCl solution at 180 seconds after the start of imaging.
Select another nematode in the chamber and measure again by steps 17–19.
Up to about 5 animals should be measured in one experiment.
Dismantle the microfluidic device after the experiment.
Clean the dismantled microfluidic device with ethanol.
Start from step 5 to continue imaging.
